answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with quadratic staked identity: each agent locks a bond tying its public key to one human-certified anchor, and payout weight grows with the square of stake while the cost grows only linearly. A grove of fresh fake agents therefore buys little influence unless the attacker also posts proportional stake for every leaf, and any detected impostor forfeits its whole bond. The shale of throwaway wallets crumbles because forging N credible identities costs N separate locked bonds plus the risk of total slashing, far above any single reward.
